newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco plans $100 mln stadium bond - paper.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco plans $100 mln stadium bond - paper.

text.p: San Francisco Mayor Willie Brown and the 49ers football team are expected to ask the Board of Supervisors on Monday to place a $100 million bond measure on the June ballot to help pay for a new stadium, according to the San Francisco Chronicle newspaper.

The Chronicle reported Friday that Brown has agreed to help finance a new $300-million-plus stadium and retail complex for the team with $100 million in lease-revenue bonds, which would be paid back with monies earned from a shopping mall the team plans to build around the stadium.
The team would pay for the rest of the stadium package with the sale of luxury boxes, tickets, advertising and other revenues generated by the project, the Chronicle reported.
If placed on the ballot, the lease-revenue bonds would only require a simple majority to pass.
San Francisco and team officials were not immediately available to comment on the report.
